clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old man presented with a 1-week history of rapidly progressive diffusely erythematous rash, initially in deep skin folds. Within 3 days, the rash spread to the trunk and extremities, forming erythematous morbilliform papules and coalescing into plaques (E001). He developed severe systemic involvement, including neutrophilic leukocytosis, acute kidney failure, metabolic and respiratory acidosis, and shock liver (E002). Initial empirical treatment with oral erythromycin and fluconazole was discontinued due to acute decompensation. Broad-spectrum antibiotics were initiated for suspected septic shock but later discontinued after infectious workup was negative (E005). With suspicion of AGEP, the patient was treated with methylprednisolone (E005). A skin biopsy was performed, which confirmed the diagnosis of AGEP by showing diffuse spongiosis and numerous subcorneal pustules filled with a mixed inflammatory infiltrate (E004).
